children: Qatari Energy Minister Saad Al-Kaabi on Sunday said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was “wrong” when he said that the strategic Strait of Hormuz will be worthless in two years.
“I mean, maybe this is his view. I think this is completely wrong,” Al-Kaabi said at the Qatar Economic Forum in New York City, according to media reports.

Bessent made the comment earlier this month, claiming that the key transit point for global oil—currently disrupted by the war with Iran—will lose its strategic relevance as nations build bypass pipelines.
“In two years, the Strait of Hormuz will be like a worthless piece of water,” Bessent said on the sidelines of a Group of 20 meeting on Sept. 1.
Prior to the war, about 20% of global oil and liquefied natural gas passed through the strait.

Al-Kaabi, who is also the chief executive officer of QatarEnergy, said that Hormuz is a key transit venue for all kinds of trade beyond oil and gas. “If you look at what the trade that we have through the Hormuz Strait, it cannot be obsolete,” he said. “If this is brought up again, I can repeat it to anybody that I don’t think this is ever going to be obsolete.”
Sheikh Faisal Al-Thani, Qatar’s minister of commerce and industry, echoed the comments by the energy minister, saying that the waterway will never be irrelevant.
